label: Roadside hearth
arrival: The kitchen caravan has stopped beside the road. The children want breakfast before the carts move: warm porridge, flatbread and something to drink.

label: Orchard dairy and bakehouse
arrival: The orchard farm offers shelter and the use of its dairy and bakehouse. Its keeper opens the dairy stores and cider cupboard for our whole stay: breakfast first, then lunch for the harvest crew.
cacheLabel: The farm’s dairy and cider stores
cacheText: Milk, cream and living cultures belong to the working dairy and cider shed. Herbs, salad leaves and oil are the farm kitchen’s stores for both meals; its churn and straining cloth remain useful equipment.

label: Market inn kitchen
arrival: Rain holds the caravan at the market inn. The innkeeper opens the vegetable pantry for supper and the following day’s lighter service. Keep our earlier bread, yogurt and dressings useful.
cacheText: Roots, onions, cooked beans, cucumber and mustard belong to the inn’s pantry. The gardener has left Evelyn’s lettuce passage with the salad supplies. These are the stocks for both hot supper and the lighter next service.

label: Market cookshop
arrival: When the rain clears, the market cookshop needs both a generous pasta lunch and filled pastries for its stall. The cook sets out the egg basket, cheese and dough-working tools for both services. Bring the inn’s roast roots and bean supper.
cacheLabel: The cookshop’s eggs, cheese and dough tools
cacheText: Eggs, grated cheese, a bread knife, a rolling pin and a cutting wheel are the cookshop’s everyday supplies. They support noodles and filled pasta, then pies and layered pastry; our flour, butter and earlier fillings come with us.

label: Community supper kitchen
arrival: The market’s community kitchen will feed the stallholders and deal with the orchard’s surplus fruit. Its vegetable basket holds cauliflower; the preserving cupboard has sugar and citrus. Bring our noodles, pastry and fruit for supper and tomorrow’s preserves.
cacheLabel: The community kitchen’s supper and preserving stores
cacheText: Cauliflower belongs to tonight’s hot supper; sugar and citrus are the preserving cupboard’s stock. One saucepan and oven serve both the savoury dishes and the fruit preserves and desserts.

label: Fair confectioner’s kitchen
arrival: The fair’s confectioner opens the kitchen for a day of sweets and custard dishes. The staff set out nuts, dates, their mortar and sugar mill, and prepared bowls of yolks and saved whites. Our sugar, pastry, bread and fruit will not go to waste.
cacheLabel: The confectioner’s nuts and custard supplies
cacheText: Almonds and dates are the confectionery stock. The cooks have already separated working bowls of yolks and whites, and set out vanilla, starch, a mortar and sugar mill. Some sugar milled for this service will be saved separately for later buttercream and icing; the saved whites will become other pastries.

label: Fair bakehouse
arrival: Next door, the fair’s baker needs filled buns and a birthday table. The baker sets out a whisk and cocoa powder; bring our eggs, butter, cream, custard, jam and caramel for both airy doughs and sponge cakes.
cacheText: The whisk serves cream and egg foams, and will remain useful for the later egg-white pastries. Cocoa powder belongs to the bakehouse’s cake supplies. The other ingredients and fillings are preparations we already know.

label: Station kitchen — tea counter
arrival: The birthday family is taking the evening train, so we bring their cakes to the station kitchen. Its cooks open the tea counter, managed dessert room and provisioning room to us. The dessert cook offers the freezing churn and pastry oven; next door, the provisioning staff prepare jars and tins beside the supper trolley. At the tea counter, cacao and baking supplies are ready for our first service.
cacheLabel: The tea-room’s chocolate and baking cupboards
cacheText: Roasted cacao nibs and cocoa butter belong to the tea-room’s chocolate work. Baking powder and baking soda are the baker’s quick-bread supplies. Our mortar, cocoa powder, cakes, cream, fruit and jam arrive with us.

label: Station kitchen — dessert room
arrival: Move to the dessert workroom in the same station kitchen. Its cook sets out the managed freezing churn and lends us the pastry oven; our earlier custards, fruit, cream and saved whites provide the food. The overnight train’s catering cart has been delayed.
cacheLabel: The dessert kitchen’s managed freezing churn
cacheText: The reusable freezing churn is the dessert cook’s equipment for custard ice, fruit sorbet and plain ice cream. The same service will finish the saved egg whites in the pastry oven.

label: Station kitchen — supper bench
arrival: At the same kitchen’s provisioning and supper bench, the cooks ask us to cover for the missing catering cart. The train needs supper now and provisions for later. The specialist’s jars, tins and opener are ready; our saved apples, bean stew, loaf, cakes and finely milled sugar provide the food. The supper trolley waits by the dining-car hatch.
cacheText: The specialist provides suitable jars, tins and an opener from the kitchen’s provisioning room. The station’s ordinary supper trolley will carry tonight’s meal and a sealed reserve. The fruit and cake ingredients are earlier supplies and preparations.
